classes.name: Tweede Kamerverkiezingen
classes.finest_note: One nationwide list-PR contest. The Kiesraad's database gives party votes by municipality for every election since 1918 (1918-1929 collected by the Kiesraad from party, municipal, and provincial archives); polling-station and candidate votes are in the EML files on data.overheid.nl from 2010 on.
classes.note: 150 members (100 until 1956) elected by open-list PR in one nationwide district; the 20 kieskringen (electoral districts) are only units for lodging lists and counting. Four-year term; the chamber can be dissolved, and early elections are frequent.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 51: De Tweede Kamer bestaat uit honderdvijftig leden; artikel 53: evenredige vertegenwoordiging)

cadence.vacancy_rule: A vacant seat passes to the next candidate on the same list (Kieswet, hoofdstuk W)

access.evidence: Party votes by municipality, province, and nation for every Tweede Kamer election since 1918, downloadable as CSV.

dates.note: First election under nationwide list PR (Grondwet 1917); the Kiesraad took the municipal figures from the SDAP's archive because the CBS published no statistics for 1918.

classes.note: Direct census-suffrage elections from the 1848 constitution: members chosen in districts by absolute majority with a runoff, half the chamber renewed every two years until 1888, then single-member districts with four-year terms; suffrage widened in 1887 and 1896. Replaced by list PR in 1918.

classes.name: Verkiezing van de Nederlandse leden van het Europees Parlement
classes.name_en: European Parliament elections in the Netherlands
classes.finest_note: One nationwide list-PR contest. Party votes by municipality since 1979 in the Kiesraad's database; polling-station and candidate votes in EML since 2009.
classes.note: The Netherlands elects its members of the European Parliament in one nationwide list-PR district on a Thursday in June (Kieswet, afdeling Y). 31 seats since 2024.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0004627 (afdeling Y: verkiezing van de leden van het Europees Parlement)

cadence.administered_by: Kiesraad (central electoral committee) with the municipal and principal electoral committees
cadence.locator: https://www.kiesraad.nl/verkiezingen/europees-parlement (Verkiezingen voor het Europees Parlement vonden voor het eerst plaats in 1979; Nederland wordt nu vertegenwoordigd door 31 leden)

access.evidence: Party votes by municipality for every European Parliament election since 1979.
EML result files with candidate and party votes by polling station for every European election since 2009.

dates.note: The Lisbon Treaty later gave the Netherlands a 26th seat, filled from this election's result (Kiesraad note).
After the United Kingdom left on 31 January 2020 the Netherlands received three more seats, filled from this election's result (Kiesraad note).

classes.name: Eerste Kamerverkiezingen
classes.finest_note: One nationwide list-PR contest among the members of the Provincial Councils and the electoral colleges, each vote weighted by population; the Kiesraad's database gives the weighted votes by province and electoral college since 2003, and EML files exist from 2011.
classes.note: 75 senators elected by the members of the twelve Provincial Councils, the three Caribbean electoral colleges, and (since 2023) the electoral college for non-residents, about two to three months after the provincial elections; votes are weighted by population (Kieswet, artikel U 2). The whole chamber has been renewed at once since 1983; before that it was renewed in parts.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 55: De leden van de Eerste Kamer worden gekozen door de leden van provinciale staten en de leden van de kiescolleges)

cadence.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 52: De zittingsduur van beide kamers is vier jaren; artikel 55)

access.evidence: Weighted votes by party per province and electoral college for the Senate elections since 2003.
EML result files for the Senate elections since 2011.

dates.note: Senate elections by the Provincial Councils before 2003 (in parts until 1983, then the whole chamber after each provincial election); not in the Kiesraad's database and not yet counted.

classes.name: Provinciale Statenverkiezingen
classes.finest_note: Party votes by municipality since 1931 in the Kiesraad's database; polling-station and candidate votes in EML from 2015. The PR elections of 1919, 1923, and 1927 are missing from the database.
classes.note: Each of the twelve Provincial Councils (eleven until 1986) is elected by list PR for four years, 39 to 55 members by population (Provinciewet artikel 8); held on the same day as the water board elections since 2015. The councils in turn elect the Senate.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 129: De leden van provinciale staten en van de gemeenteraad worden rechtstreeks gekozen)

cadence.administered_by: Kiesraad (central electoral committee) with the municipal and principal electoral committees
cadence.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0004627 (artikel C 4: De leden van provinciale staten, de algemene besturen, onderscheidenlijk gemeenteraden worden gekozen voor vier jaren)

access.evidence: Party votes by municipality and province for every Provincial Council election since 1931.
EML result files with candidate and party votes by polling station since 2015.

dates.note: The list-PR provincial elections of 1919, 1923, and 1927 are not in the Kiesraad's database; not yet counted.

classes.name: Provinciale Statenverkiezingen in kiesdistricten (1850-1917)
classes.note: Before list PR, provincial councillors were chosen in districts by majority vote under the Provinciewet of 1850, with partial renewals.
classes.disposition_reason: No official body publishes these district results; they survive only in the provincial archives and the provincial gazettes, which are not digitized as results.

classes.name: Gemeenteraadsverkiezingen
classes.finest_note: Party votes by municipality since 1931 in the Kiesraad's database, including reorganization, postponed, and new elections; polling-station and candidate votes in EML from 2012 (the 2022 general set is the Kiesraad's pre-publication of the municipalities' own files). The PR elections of 1919, 1923, and 1927 are missing.
classes.note: Every municipal council is elected by list PR for four years, all on one day in March; a municipality formed by a merger elects its new council in November before the merger takes effect (herindelingsverkiezing), and its next regular election may be skipped. Non-Dutch residents may vote under conditions.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 129: De leden van provinciale staten en van de gemeenteraad worden rechtstreeks gekozen)

access.evidence: Party votes by municipality for every general municipal election since 1931 and the reorganization elections in between.
EML result files with candidate and party votes by polling station since the 2012 reorganization elections.

classes.name: Gemeenteraadsverkiezingen in kiesdistricten (1851-1917)
classes.note: Under the Gemeentewet of 1851 councillors were chosen by majority vote, in larger towns by district, with a third of each council renewed every two years.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were kept by each of the roughly 1,100 municipalities; no official compilation exists, and the municipal archives are not digitized as results.

classes.name: Waterschapsverkiezingen (algemeen bestuur)
classes.finest_note: Party votes by water board and municipality since 2015 in the Kiesraad's database; polling-station and candidate votes in EML from 2015. The first list election, by post in November 2008, is not in the database.
classes.note: Residents elect most of each water board's general board (algemeen bestuur) by list PR for four years, on the same day as the provincial elections since 2015; the seats for unbuilt land and nature areas are appointed by designated organizations (Waterschapswet artikelen 12-14) and are not elected.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0005108 (artikel 12: categorieën van belanghebbenden; artikel 14: de vertegenwoordigers van de categorieën b en c worden benoemd)

cadence.administered_by: Kiesraad (central electoral committee) with the municipal and principal electoral committees
cadence.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0004627 (artikel C 4: De leden van provinciale staten, de algemene besturen, onderscheidenlijk gemeenteraden worden gekozen voor vier jaren)

access.evidence: Party votes by water board and municipality for the water board elections since 2015.
EML result files (published as AB, algemeen bestuur) with candidate and party votes by polling station since 2015.

dates.note: First list election of the water boards, by postal vote in November 2008; not in the Kiesraad's database and not yet counted.

classes.name: Waterschapsverkiezingen vóór 2008 (personenstelsel)
classes.note: Before 2008 each water board elected its board members as persons, by category of stakeholders (residents, owners, and businesses), under its own regulations, often by post and with low turnout.
classes.disposition_reason: Each board ran and recorded its own elections; no official body compiled or publishes the results, and the boards themselves have since merged into 21.

classes.name: Eilandsraadsverkiezingen
classes.finest_note: Party and candidate votes per island from the official reports (processen-verbaal); polling-station figures only for the 2020 Sint Eustatius election. The 2023 results are CSV files on data.overheid.nl, not yet in the database.
classes.note: Bonaire (9 seats), Sint Eustatius (5), and Saba (5) each elect an island council by list PR for four years, on the provincial election day; non-Dutch residents of five years' legal residence may vote.
classes.locator: https://www.kiesraad.nl/verkiezingen/eilandsraden (De eilandsraad ... wordt ook net als die raad voor 4 jaar rechtstreeks gekozen; Bonaire: 9 zetels, Sint Eustatius: 5 zetels, Saba: 5 zetels)

cadence.administered_by: The central electoral committee of each island, chaired by the gezaghebber
cadence.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0004627 (afdeling Ya, § 3: De verkiezing van de leden van de eilandsraad)

access.evidence: Party and candidate votes per island from the official reports, 2011-2023.
De uitslagen van de eilandsraad en kiescolleges van 15 maart 2023 ... zijn in CSV-formaat gepubliceerd op data.overheid.nl.

dates.note: Sint Eustatius did not vote: its island council had been dissolved under the 2018 intervention act.
Sint Eustatius only, after the intervention.

classes.name: Verkiezing van de kiescolleges voor de Eerste Kamer (Bonaire, Sint Eustatius en Saba)
classes.finest_note: Party and candidate votes per island from the official reports in the Kiesraad's database (2019 and 2023).
classes.note: Since 2019 the voters of each Caribbean public body directly elect an electoral college (kiescollege) whose only task is to vote in the Senate election, as the Provincial Councils do in the European Netherlands; elected on the provincial election day.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 132a, derde lid, with artikel 55: de leden van de kiescolleges)

cadence.administered_by: The central electoral committee of each island
cadence.locator: https://www.kiesraad.nl/verkiezingen/kiescolleges (Voor de verkiezingen in Caribisch Nederland is ieder eiland één kieskring; per eiland één centraal stembureau)

access.evidence: Party and candidate votes per island from the official reports (P 22-2).

dates.note: Bonaire, Saba, and Sint Eustatius; the same page also holds the non-resident college.

classes.name: Verkiezing van het kiescollege niet-ingezetenen
classes.finest_note: One contest; party and candidate votes from the official report (P 22-3) in the Kiesraad's database.
classes.note: Dutch citizens living abroad who register with The Hague elect, by post only, an electoral college of 9 to 55 members (25 in 2023) that votes in the Senate election. First held in 2023.
classes.locator: https://www.kiesraad.nl/verkiezingen/kiescolleges (Kiescollege niet-ingezetenen; Voor de Eerste Kamerverkiezing van 2023 telde het kiescollege niet-ingezetenen 25 leden; Kiezers kunnen alleen per brief stemmen)

cadence.administered_by: Municipality of The Hague (postal voting office) and the central electoral committee for non-residents
cadence.locator: https://www.kiesraad.nl/verkiezingen/kiescolleges (Het centraal stembureau is gevestigd in Zuid-Holland; de burgemeester van Den Haag)

access.evidence: Party and candidate votes for the non-resident electoral college from the official report (P 22-3).

classes.name: Nationale referenda
classes.finest_note: Votes by municipality in the Kiesraad's database for all three; polling-station counts in EML for 2016 and 2018.
classes.note: Three national referendums, all non-binding: 2005 (consultative, by a one-off act) and 2016 and 2018 (advisory, under the Wet raadgevend referendum of 2015, repealed with effect to 10 July 2018). The constitution has no binding referendum.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0036443 (Regeling vervallen per 12-07-2018 met terugwerkende kracht tot en met 10-07-2018)

access.evidence: Votes for and against by municipality for the 2005, 2016, and 2018 referendums.
EML result files with counts by polling station for the 2016 and 2018 advisory referendums.

dates.note: Consultative referendum on the treaty establishing a Constitution for Europe, under its own act.
Advisory referendum under the Wet raadgevend referendum on the EU-Ukraine Association Agreement.
Advisory referendum under the Wet raadgevend referendum on the Intelligence and Security Services Act 2017; held with the municipal elections.

classes.name: Wijkraden en stadsdeelcommissies
classes.finest_note: Published by each municipality, not by the Kiesraad: Rotterdam posts its neighborhood council results on its own site; Amsterdam's borough committee results come from its research office.
classes.note: Under Gemeentewet artikel 83 a council may set up district committees; Amsterdam's stadsdeelcommissies and Rotterdam's 37 wijkraden and 2 dorpsraden (7 to 11 members each) are elected directly on the municipal election day. They replaced the borough councils abolished in 2014.
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0005416 (artikel 83: De raad ... kan bestuurscommissies instellen)

cadence.locator: https://www.rotterdam.nl/wijkraden (Op 22 april 2026 zijn de nieuwe wijk- en dorpsraadsleden geïnstalleerd)

access.evidence: The wijkraden page links to the neighborhood council results (Uitslagen) and a map of the districts.

classes.name: Deelraadsverkiezingen (stadsdeelraden en deelgemeenteraden)
classes.note: Amsterdam's stadsdeelraden and Rotterdam's deelgemeenteraden were directly elected borough councils with delegated powers, elected with the municipal councils; abolished in 2014 when the Gemeentewet dropped the deelgemeente.
classes.disposition_reason: Results were published only by the two municipalities; amsterdam.nl refuses automated requests and Rotterdam's archive of these results was not located on its site, so no source is reachable yet.

classes.name: Gemeentelijke referenda
classes.note: Municipalities may hold advisory or consultative referendums under their own referendum ordinances, made under their general power to regulate (Gemeentewet artikel 147); the results bind no one.
classes.disposition_reason: Each municipality runs and publishes its own referendums; the Kiesraad keeps no register or results, so there is no official list to start from.

classes.name: Provinciale referenda
classes.note: A province may hold an advisory referendum under its own ordinance (Provinciewet artikel 143); none is recorded centrally.
classes.disposition_reason: No official register of provincial referendums exists; any results sit with the province that held one.

classes.name: Raadplegend burgemeestersreferendum
classes.note: For some years after 2001 the Gemeentewet let a council put its two shortlisted mayoral candidates to a consultative vote of the residents before recommending one; the provision has since been repealed and the mayor is appointed (artikel 61).
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0005416 (artikel 61: De burgemeester wordt bij koninklijk besluit ... benoemd voor de tijd van zes jaar)
classes.disposition_reason: The few votes held were run and published by the municipalities themselves; no official central record lists them.

classes.name: Koning
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 24: Het koningschap wordt erfelijk vervuld)
classes.disposition_reason: The King is head of state by hereditary succession (Grondwet artikel 24); no election.

classes.name: Commissaris van de Koning
classes.locator: https://wetten.overheid.nl/BWBR0001840 (artikel 131: De commissaris van de Koning en de burgemeester worden aangesteld)
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the Crown (Grondwet artikel 131); no election.

classes.name: Burgemeester
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by royal decree for six years on the council's recommendation (Gemeentewet artikel 61); no election.

classes.name: Gezaghebber
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by royal decree (Wet openbare lichamen BES); no election.

classes.name: Dijkgraaf
classes.disposition_reason: Appointed by the Crown on the board's recommendation (Waterschapswet); no election.

classes.name: Wethouders, gedeputeerden en dagelijkse besturen
classes.disposition_reason: Aldermen, provincial executives, island deputies, and water board executives are appointed by their councils from their own resolutions; the archive records councils, not these appointments.

classes.name: Tweede Kamer gekozen door Provinciale Staten (1815-1848)
classes.name_en: House of Representatives chosen by the Provincial States (1815-1848)
classes.disposition_reason: Before 1848 the Provincial States chose the members, who were themselves chosen through estates; no popular vote, and the Kiesraad's records start with the first direct election of 1848.

classes.name: Rechterlijke macht
classes.disposition_reason: Judges are appointed for life by royal decree (Grondwet artikel 117); no judicial elections.

classes.name: Kandidaatstelling binnen partijen
classes.disposition_reason: Parties select candidates and list leaders internally (member ballots in some parties); the state runs no primaries and publishes no results. Lists are lodged under Kieswet hoofdstuk H.

classes.name: Ondernemingsraden en medezeggenschapsraden
classes.disposition_reason: Works councils, school participation councils, and similar bodies are elected inside private and public institutions under sector laws; no official body publishes results.
